title: AI for HR and People Processes

questions.question: Why do HR AI use cases need stricter controls?
options: They mostly reformat existing policy text, so the wording is the only thing at stake
They can involve personal data, fairness, employee impact, and manager accountability
They run on internal HR systems, where the data has already cleared privacy review
They are drafted by HR specialists, whose expertise catches any error before it spreads
questions.explanation: HR workflows often affect employees directly and require clear human accountability. Privacy, fairness, and employee trust have to be designed into the workflow from the start.

questions.question: An AI tool scores internal candidates during a promotion round. What does this lesson's legal frame say applies?
options: It stays outside the AI Act because the model only ranks and a manager makes the final call, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases
It is exempt while the tool runs internally and its outputs never leave the company
It only needs a data processing agreement, since personal data stays in the HR system
Annex III of the EU AI Act covers it as high-risk employment use, so human oversight applies
questions.explanation: The lesson places recruitment, evaluation, promotion, termination, and performance-monitoring use cases under Annex III, point 4 of the EU AI Act, where conformity assessment and human oversight apply. Where an output drives a decision with legal or similarly significant effect without meaningful human review, Art. 22 GDPR is engaged as well.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
options: A personnel decision that the responsible manager can confirm with one click
A payroll integration that writes the outcome back into the HR system
A legal approval that clears the use case under the EU AI Act
A ranked HR AI triage plan with matched controls and rationale
questions.explanation: The artifact supports triage and control selection. It does not make HR decisions - humans own judgment, decisions, employee communication, and sensitive escalations.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
options: A named human decision owner who carries the people decision, not the model
A privacy exemption for HR data, since employees already consented at hiring
A fairness check deferred until the first complaint reaches the works council
A communication script that avoids saying where AI was used in the process
questions.explanation: A human decision owner is required for people-related decisions. Privacy review, fairness checks, and a communication script are the other controls this lesson teaches.

questions.question: When should an HR AI use case require a launch gate?
options: Only when the workflow touches recruitment rather than internal learning paths
Only when the works council has already asked for the tool to be reviewed
Only when the output is sent to employees rather than kept inside the HR team
When employee impact, personal data sensitivity, and uncertainty are high
questions.explanation: High-impact HR use cases need explicit review before rollout, driven by employee impact, data sensitivity, and uncertainty rather than by who has already objected.

questions.question: What should communication clarify in HR AI workflows?
options: Where AI supports the work and where humans still make the decision
How the model was trained and which vendor supplied the underlying system
Which HR processes were the fastest to automate during the pilot phase
How much reviewer time the workflow saved compared with the manual process
questions.explanation: Trust depends on clear boundaries between AI support and human accountability. Employee trust is treated as a design requirement, not a communications afterthought.
